title: Mum's Oldest (Wilma McIvor)
style: folk country acoustic guitar warm female vocal 98bpm brushed drums gentle storytelling intimate unhurried
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
He came first, and that changes a person
You carry the weight of the ones who come after
I watched him on rooftops and I held my breath
But he was sure-footed, always was

[Verse 2]
When he rang to say he was buying the boat
I made a cup of tea and sat for a while
Your father laughed — of course he did, of course
That's the boy who never stayed still

[Chorus]
My oldest one, the one who led the way
My oldest one, I see him in the early day
Standing at the water, looking for the line
My oldest one — I'm glad you're doing fine

[Bridge]
I sent him twenty-three birthday photos last year
Three of them were Pete instead of Corey
He said — Mum, that's not me, that's the wrong one
I know love, but I wanted you to feel seen too

[Verse 3]
He runs his boats and I run my garden
Different kinds of captain, same steady hands
His father's in his posture, mine in his patience
The oldest son carries what no-one understands

[Outro]
The gardens still growing
The gardens still growing
My oldest one
The gardens still growing
